full_judgment:
9. Perused the material on record. The plaintiffs produced the deed on sale dated 6-5-1959 (Exhibit-1). They also produced the Registered Ekrarnama executed by the predecessor of the defendants (Exhibit-2), It appears from the said Ekrarnama that it was executed on the same date, written by the same scribe and attested by same witnesses and further it appears that no specific date of repayment of consideration money was mentioned in the said deed. The Ekrarnama (Exhibit- 2) is a registered deed carrying usual presumption of its validity. In support of the execution of the aforesaid Ekrarnama besides PW 1 (plaintiff No.1) PW 2 Md Yaseen was also examined who deposed that he was present at the time of execution of the aforesaid Ekrarnama. There is nothing in the cross-examination of this witness to disbelieve him nor there is any enmity between this witness and the defendants and there is no suggestion even to this witness of any enmity and, as such, I have no reason to disbelieve the claim of genuineness of the Ekrarnama on the basis of evidence produced in this behalf. The defence version is that by misleading the predecessor of the defendants namely, Jamir Hossain the deed was obtained from him. I have considered evidence of DWs in this connection. The defendant failed to point out any material to indicate that he was either illiterate or otherwise simpleton man. On the contrary, it appears that he was serving as a clerk in the police office and was sufficiently educated man and, as such, the story of obtaining the deed, registered duly, from the aforesaid predecessor of the defendants by misleading him cannot be believed. The trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court, on the basis of the evidence, found the document to be genuine. There is no misreading or non consideration of any evidence and, as such, I do not find any reason to differ with such concurrent finding of fact. 

 13. It appears from the above provision of law that Government is a necessary party in a suit for specific performance of contract. It appears that the intention of the legislature to include the above provision in the law is to stop transfers of immovable property in contravention of any law of the land. Non impleading simpliciter in a suit of the present nature would, in my opinion, not invalidate the decree and moreover, in the instant suit there being no such grievance raised at any time earlier at any stage of the trial the decree cannot be found fault with, on this ground alone, if it is found otherwise sustainable. 

 14. In this connection a decision reported in the case of Asadunnessa and others vs Kamruzzaman and others reported in 26 DLR 363 may be referred to though the facts of the said case are not similar to those of the present case. In the said decision DC Bhattacharya J, as he was then, after considering the preamble of President's Order No. 142 of 1972 held "the obvious object of the legislation as is found in the preamble of the order and also in its substantive provisions appears to be prevention of certain transfers of immovable property in derogation of some legislative enactments. It therefore, may be held that mere non- impleading of the Government in the suit does not non suit the plaintiffs automatically. More so the objection being not raised at any previous stage nor the defendants-petitioners could point out that by non-impleading the Government any failure of justice has occasioned nor any transfer is sought for avoiding any law. There is therefore no failure of justice on this score. 

 "9. No suit shall be defeated by reason of the misjoinder or non-joinder of parties, and the Court may in every suit deal with the matter in controversy so far as regards the rights and interest of the parties actually before it." 

 16. In spite of the Government being not joined as a party in the suit, the Courts below dealt with the matter of controversy so far as regards the right and interest of both the parties and, as such, I hold that by mere non-joinder of the Government the suit cannot be defeated. The learned Advocate for the defendant petitioners lastly submits that the Ekrarnama even if believed to be a genuine document was executed in 1959 and now with the passage of time, the defendants cannot be bound to recover the property on the same consideration fixed in 1959.
